dedupe_keys.name: chemical release risk assessment in an earthquake refinery h2s natech scenario heliyon 2024

description: This case study assesses the risk that an earthquake damages a refinery and releases hydrogen sulphide (H2S), a toxic gas, as a Natech event, a technological accident triggered by a natural hazard. It follows the first three links of the disaster chain: damage to chemical facilities, release of chemicals and their dispersion. Seismic hazard parameters for the fault near the refinery, such as moment magnitude, focal depth and peak ground acceleration and velocity, were derived from past earthquakes, and a vessel processing H2S at 98% concentration was selected. It was written by Parvin Shafiei-Moghaddam, Katayoun Jahangiri and Nemat Hassani of institutions in Tehran and published in Heliyon (volume 10, issue 8, e28797) in April 2024. Coverage is a single refinery site. The article is available online free as open access under CC BY-NC 4.0 in PubMed Central. Method and finding: a semi-quantitative assessment with the RAPID-N software showed the highest-probability scenario releasing H2S over a radius of 6.59 km from the vessel under stable atmospheric conditions. Caveats: the method is semi-quantitative and rests on one vessel and assumed weather, and the parts read do not name the refinery. For simulation it is a worked example of chaining a seismic hazard model, equipment damage and toxic dispersion, useful for emergency response planning around process plants. It is related to the RAPID-N model record in this catalogue, the tool it used.
